CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Paul Edwards is a 59-year-old HIV-positive male presenting for hypogonadism follow-up. Patient was last seen on November 24, 2020. He is currently on testosterone replacement therapy 1 ml every 10 days (current dose 140 mg), initiated when his testosterone levels were less than 300 ng/dL. He reports feeling well on therapy with improved vigor, energy, and sleep quality. He has noted positive changes in his bloodwork, particularly significant improvement in lipid panel with triglycerides decreasing from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL over 5 months since starting testosterone. He reports his red blood cell count has increased and is stable. Patient denies weight loss and states he is maintaining his usual physique. He is compliant with medications and uses a medication calendar to track his testosterone injections, currently on day 8 of his cycle, due for next injection Thursday or Friday. Patient asked about indole-3-carbinol/broccoli extract for estrogen control but was counseled that his estradiol levels are not elevated. Patient also requested increase in testosterone dose to 175 mg, but this was discussed in detail regarding risks. Doctor counseled patient that his testosterone peaks have been greater than 1,500 ng/dL, which increases risk of polycythemia and potential need to discontinue therapy. Given his current well-being and good lab values, decision made to maintain current dose rather than escalate.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for improved vigor and sleep. Negative for weight loss or other constitutional symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV infection
Hypogonadism
History of hypertriglyceridemia

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone 1 ml every 10 days (140 mg)
Finasteride 5 mg daily (taking half dose)
Cialis 5 mg on workout days, 2.5 mg on other days (recently ran out)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works out regularly. Uses Walmart pharmacy. Maintains medication calendar for tracking testosterone injections. Reports taking steps to improve his overall health and life situation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Trim appearance
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no concerns
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no concerns

RESULTS
Triglycerides: 145 mg/dL (previous 265 mg/dL)
Red blood cell count: Increased, stable
PSA: 0.6 ng/mL (previous 0.5 ng/mL, normal <4 ng/mL)
Testosterone: Previously >1,500 ng/dL; current levels on day 8 of injection cycle not documented
Estradiol: Not elevated (previously checked)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
59-year-old HIV-positive male with hypogonadism, well-controlled on testosterone replacement therapy with excellent response. Lipid panel significantly improved. PSA and other labs reassuring. Patient counseled against dose escalation due to high testosterone peaks and associated risks of polycythemia, which could necessitate discontinuation of therapy. Current dose is appropriate and patient is feeling well. Maintain current testosterone dose at 1 ml every 10 days. Continue finasteride 5 mg daily at current dose (half pill). Continue cialis as prescribed. Refill prescriptions for testosterone, finasteride, and cialis; patient prefers paper prescriptions. May recheck testosterone and estradiol in fall if desired. PSA to be rechecked annually. Patient expressed understanding and agreement with plan.
